summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for chronic G-tube site pain due to mechanical pulling of the tube, which failed to resolve with prior interventions. She underwent an open gastrostomy tube replacement without complications. Postoperatively, she remained stable, afebrile, and alert, with good pain control managed initially with PCA and transitioned to oral Dilaudid via G-tube. Tube feeds were restarted on postoperative day 2 and advanced to her prior rate of 65 mL/hour, which she tolerated well. She resumed sipping water, ambulated early, and had no signs of infection or bleeding. A MRSA screen was negative. She was discharged home with home health services for wound care, instructions to crush all medications and administer via G-tube, and clear guidance on activity restrictions, diet, and warning signs. Follow-up was arranged with her surgeon.
